<!-- clinicos-review-handoff:v1 -->
{
  "kind": "report",
  "actor": "l2v-hub",
  "pr": 498,
  "subject_sha": "23eacd2a5672c5e8d713417ef2c6a82bbba004fe",
  "request_id": "01117de6-d8d3-41ae-9bc9-81eb12cb96fd",
  "claim_id": "5a45cc90-909c-49c6-9cc8-0edef100ac21",
  "round": 2,
  "report": {
    "subject_sha": "23eacd2a5672c5e8d713417ef2c6a82bbba004fe",
    "verdict": "changes-requested",
    "summary": "Round-3 low finding (RAILWAY_DEMO_TOKEN possibly a repository-level secret) is RESOLVED. I checked names-only metadata (read-only, no values): GET repos/l2v-hub/ClinicOS/actions/secrets lists ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN_*, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, CLINICOS_BOT_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, RAILWAY_TOKEN, VERCEL_TOKEN, and RAILWAY_DEMO_TOKEN is not among them. The 'glistening-friendship / demo' environment lists RAILWAY_DEMO_TOKEN, with custom_branch_policies=true and a single branch policy 'main'. The owner is a User account, so there is no organization-secret scope. Run 39729875897 (Protect demo secret scope, workflow_dispatch on main@b062de33) succeeded: preflight, ensure_environment_copy and remove_repository_copy all passed. Run 39730182635 (inspect-ambient-availability) also succeeded. Commit b062de33 (#499) is merged to main. protect-demo-secret.yml, protect-demo-secret.mjs, protect-demo-secret.test.mjs and evidence/gh-cli-v2.103.0.md are blob-identical at 23eacd2a5, 3436d6c9 (#499) and main b062de33, so I did not re-review them. The application code at 23eacd2a5 is identical to source 42ecd1f9 (the diff excluding artifacts is empty), which matches the packet-11 binding. CI on 23eacd2a5: archive-tests, browser-e2e, bug-pipeline-tests, frontend-tests, gate, real-provider, secret-scan and windows-review-setup pass. Vercel fails on a rate limit, which is tolerated. Packet 11 and the complete-demo-release-flow QA describe local-only verification (focused 423 pass, full 1072 pass with 3 skipped, 8 adversarial). No real exact dispatch, preflight or deploy has been run. I did not run any tests. The new integration is sound on the security and safety points I checked. (1) The release job alone gains actions:write. The dispatch uses github.token via BUG_PIPELINE_ACTIONS_TOKEN, with GH_TOKEN overridden and GITHUB_TOKEN dropped. It POSTs to one literal endpoint with ref=main, and the inputs are restricted to {reviewed_sha, operation, dispatch_id}. Output is bounded, there are no retries, and the error is fixed and never echoes stderr. (2) The job if-guards and release.mjs main() require repo l2v-hub/ClinicOS, ref main, and the fixed workflow_ref and event. The exact workflow asserts reviewed_sha==GITHUB_SHA, ref main and the fixed workflow_ref before the demo token step, and the demo environment is branch-restricted to main. A PR or non-main ref therefore cannot obtain the demo token. (3) Race safety holds. currentMain is checked before and after the POST, during polling and after artifact retrieval. The run identity check covers display_title, head_sha, path, event, branch, attempt 1 and that the run is not among prior IDs. A main move fails closed with no redispatch. (4) Intent is persisted before the single POST. Resume never re-POSTs. deployDemo with the exact policy requires an idle inventory and reuses an already-active identical commit, so there is no double deploy or migration from retries. The trigger and exact policies are mutually exclusive (1 vs 0 Railway triggers), so the push-triggered deploy-backend demo job cannot deploy alongside the exact path. (5) The merge gates are unchanged: verifyCurrentCandidate (reviews, required checks, evidence, ledger), squash with --match-head-commit, and no admin or force. The exact preflight runs before the merge and again inside the merge guard. Recording requires the durable succeeded deploy dispatch, a matching runUrl and the receipt digest, and the live verify is re-checked against current main and attempt 1. (6) Concurrency: the release queue (codex-bug-pipeline) is separate from railway-demo, and the production deploy-backend job stays in railway-backend. Actions are pinned in the new and changed steps, persist-credentials is false, and the exact workflow runs credential-free tests before secrets. Evidence limits are shared at 32 MiB binary and 48 MiB transport, with canonical base64 and Git blob SHA-1 checks. Remaining issues: (a) MEDIUM. Saved exact dispatch progress has no recovery path. Any main movement, preflight expiry (24h) or failed demo run permanently blocks the batch, including after merge and in record/publication. (b) MEDIUM. In exact mode, the backend release no longer requires RAILWAY_TOKEN and no longer waits for the push-triggered production deploy-backend run (prisma migrate deploy). Issues can be closed while the production backend deploy failed. (c) LOW. The deploy-backend.yml demo job with the trigger policy will deterministically fail its preflight on every backend push once the demo service is in exact configuration (0 triggers).",
    "findings": [
      {
        "severity": "medium",
        "file": "agent-team/src/bug-pipeline/exact-demo-dispatch.mjs",
        "line": 114,
        "problem": "Saved progress is bound forever to the SHA of main at dispatch time. ensure() fails when progress.sha differs from current main ('saved dispatch identity mismatch'), and any non-success run fails with 'no redispatch'. Nothing in release.mjs (ensureExact at lines 414-438, the merged-recovery branch at line 491, verifyReleaseDemo checkMain at lines 35-46, record and publishDeploymentCompletion) ever clears or supersedes batch.exactDemoDispatches. Several common cases therefore leave a batch stuck with no supported way out: another PR merges to main between preflight and merge; the saved preflight receipt passes its 24h expiry; a transient Railway failure fails the deploy run; main moves during the up-to-60-minute runtime wait before confirm-demo runs record. After a merge, the code is on main and demo-deployed state is unknown, yet source issues stay open with no status explaining why. Recovery requires hand-editing durable state. release.test.mjs:1624 confirms that a post-merge main move fails every retry.",
        "requested_change": "Add an explicit, authorized recovery transition. For example, on a definitive failure (main moved, preflight expired, run failed) record a releaseHold or blocked status with a fixed code in durable state, and publish a sanitized status on the PR and source issues. Provide a guarded operator action that archives the stale dispatch progress (keeping its run IDs in priorRunIds) so that a fresh preflight can run against the current main, or, post-merge, a deploy of current main that is verified to contain mergeSha as an ancestor and is re-preflighted. A plain re-run must never redispatch.",
        "test_expectation": "Tests where: (1) main moves after a successful preflight but before the merge; (2) the saved preflight is older than 24h; (3) the deploy run concludes with failure; (4) main moves before record. Each must produce a durable blocked state plus a sanitized issue/PR status with no second POST on plain retry. After the authorized recovery action, exactly one new dispatch is made with a new dispatch_id, prior run IDs are excluded, and the release completes or fails closed with issues open."
      },
      {
        "severity": "medium",
        "file": "agent-team/src/bug-pipeline/release.mjs",
        "line": 353,
        "problem": "With sourcePolicy native-exact-commit-v1, a backend change no longer requires RAILWAY_TOKEN to be configured. codex-bug-release.yml (line 111) also removed the step that waited for the deploy-backend.yml run of merge_sha. That push-triggered workflow still deploys production Railway (job 'deploy', railway up with prisma migrate deploy). As a result, the release records 'deployed' and closes source issues on demo-only proof, even when the production backend deploy (including migrations) failed or never ran. Before this change, its success was a prerequisite (railway_url came from that run). This weakens a release gate silently, and the completion comment's 'Deploy Railway riuscito' link now points to the demo run only.",
        "requested_change": "Either keep requiring RAILWAY_TOKEN for backend changes and await and verify the deploy-backend.yml 'deploy' job for merge_sha (completed, success, head_sha == merge_sha, attempt 1, path and event bound) before recording or closing, or document and test an explicit owner decision that production backend deploy is out of scope, and make the completion text say demo-only.",
        "test_expectation": "A release test with deployments.backend and the exact policy, where the production deploy-backend run for mergeSha fails or is missing: the batch is not recorded as deployed, issues stay open, and a sanitized failure status is published. A configured=false railway case with the exact policy is rejected before merge, unless the documented decision says otherwise."
      },
      {
        "severity": "low",
        "file": ".github/workflows/deploy-backend.yml",
        "line": 74,
        "problem": "The push-triggered 'demo' job still runs 'demo-deployment.mjs preflight' with the default trigger policy. That policy's validateTarget requires exactly one Railway deployment trigger, while the exact path this PR makes mandatory requires zero. Once the demo service is in exact configuration, every backend push to main will fail this job, making 'Deploy Backend to Railway' red even when production deployed fine. That masks real production failures and confuses operators who watch this run.",
        "requested_change": "Remove or disable the trigger-policy demo job in deploy-backend.yml (or gate it on the configured policy) now that native-exact-commit-v1 is the release path, keeping the production 'deploy' job unchanged.",
        "test_expectation": "A workflow-structure test asserting that deploy-backend.yml has no job using RAILWAY_DEMO_TOKEN with the trigger policy (or that it is gated off under the exact policy), and that the exact workflow is the only demo deployer."
      }
    ]
  }
}
